claim.pdf_says: "D.6.1.2   Runtime level organization" and "D.6.1.3   EXAMPLE" are printed at the same typographic rank as "D.6.1.1   Source level organization" on the preceding page (1071) - all three are fourth-level clauses under D.6.1.
claim.markdown_says: ## D.6.1.2 Runtime level organization  ...  ## D.6.1.3 EXAMPLE   (while page 1071 has '#### D.6.1.1 Source level organization' and '### D.6.1 Compilation group and run unit organization')
claim.why_it_matters: Siblings D.6.1.1, D.6.1.2 and D.6.1.3 land at different markdown levels, so D.6.1.2 and D.6.1.3 are hoisted out of D.6.1 and appear as peers of D.6 itself. Any TOC, outline fold, or section-extraction script driven off heading depth mis-parents them.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. The markdown heading levels are quoted accurately (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 42983 '### D.6.1', 42988 '#### D.6.1.1', 43127 '## D.6.1.2', 43136 '## D.6.1.3'), but the claim is not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy, on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING - kind=missing-heading is a misnomer. Both headings are present verbatim on page 1075 with their exact printed clause numbers and titles ('D.6.1.2 Runtime level organization', 'D.6.1.3 EXAMPLE'), and so is every word of their body text. (2) THE CLAIM'S PDF EVIDENCE IS MEASURABLY FALSE. I extracted the PDF span metrics with PyMuPDF for both pages. Every Annex-D heading on both pages is set in the IDENTICAL face and size - Cambria,Bold 11.67pt: p1071 y=127.18 'D.6', y=240.01 'D.6.1', y=290.58 'D.6.1.1'; p1075 y=90.21 'D.6.1.2', y=216.66 'D.6.1.3' (the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' is also 11.67pt Cambria,Bold). The rendered 300dpi images agree visually. So D.6.1.2 is at the same typographic rank as D.6.1.1 ONLY in the vacuous sense that it is equally at the same typographic rank as D.6 and D.6.1. This PDF encodes NO typographic level distinction among annex clauses at all; there is no rank property in the source that the markdown could have lost. Depth is carried solely by the dotted clause number, which the transcription reproduces exactly and correctly. (3) MEANING IS UNCHANGED. 'D.6.1.2' self-declares its parent as D.6.1 to any human reader and to any number-driven parser, independent of the '#' count. No COBOL syntax, semantics, or normative content is affected - this is Annex D (informative, 'Concepts'). (4) NOT A PAGE-1075 FACT, BUT GLOBAL MARKUP SCAFFOLDING. I checked all 305 'D.*' headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: 243 of them have a markdown level that differs from their numeric depth, and Annex D is globally offset besides (D.1 and D.2 are second-level clauses yet sit at '###'). The '##' demotion is an artifact of the transcription's per-page markup generator - D.6.1.2 sits 5 lines below the '## Page 1075' scaffold marker - and 50 of the mismatches occur directly after a page marker. Page 1075 is in no way special. Under the stated rejection criteria this is 'only page-break furniture / formatting' and 'does not change meaning'.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy; reject as a page-1075 ledger entry. The accurate underlying observation is a repository-wide markup-hygiene issue, not a transcription-fidelity one: specs/ISO_COBOL.md does not normalize markdown heading depth to ISO clause depth anywhere in Annex D - 243 of 305 'D.*' headings have '#'-count != dotted-number depth, and the whole annex is additionally offset by one (D.1/D.2 at '###'). The '##' seen at D.6.1.2 and D.6.1.3 is the generator resetting depth at a page boundary. The PDF cannot arbitrate this: PyMuPDF shows every Annex-D heading on pages 1071 and 1075 printed in one uniform Cambria,Bold 11.67pt, so the PDF asserts no heading hierarchy beyond the clause numbers themselves - which the markdown already carries correctly. If the owner wants outline-driven tooling to work, the fix is a single global pass deriving '#'-count from the dotted number across all 305 Annex-D headings (and the equivalent elsewhere), tracked as a docs/tooling task - not 305 per-page reconciliation findings, and not one filed against page 1075.
